items.title: Michigan’s Mike Rogers says trade war with Canada needs to end
items.standfirst: Weeks after he called for an end to the war with Iran, the GOP Senate candidate is breaking with the Trump administration again.
items.content: Michigan Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers called for an end to the “tariff war” with Canada in a new campaign advertisement released Wednesday, another break from the Trump administration weeks before the midterm elections.Rogers’ ad comes as Republican campaign groups across the country have entered triage mode in an effort to salvage GOP control in an unfavorable political environment.“Here in Michigan, we know that Canada is not our enemy. We need to end this tariff war now,” Rogers said in the advertisement, which is part of a coordinated spend between his campaign at the National Republican Senatorial Committee.He added, “as Michigan’s senator, I’ll bring both parties together to lower your prices.”Each year, Michigan does roughly $80 billion in trade with Canada, according to the Michigan Chamber of Commerce.The new video comes weeks after he put out another advertisement breaking with President Donald Trump, publicly calling for the war with Iran to end “quickly.”In both commercials, Rogers said that prices are too high and neither mentioned the president by name.The latest ad is a shift from his previous positioning on trade with Canada.Last month, Rogers said that some of the tariffs imposed on Canadian goods are needed, as the state’s manufacturing sector has been gutted by cheap foreign imports in the past.“President Trump is right to put America first — and tariffs are necessary, but are not a one-size-fits-all solution,” Rogers previously said in a press release.But, he also said he has the pull to end the trade war threatening Michigan.During a press conference in the Oval Office on Wednesday, Trump downplayed the suggestion that Rogers was breaking with him."I viewed him as saying that he thinks Canada should make a deal," Trump said. "Canada has been ripping off our country for many, many years."Rogers’ and Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed’s campaigns did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
